territorial_scope.description: Applies to exports, reexports and in-country transfers of items subject to U.S. jurisdiction, reaching destinations in and outside the UAE; UAE access to advanced computing items and STA is targeted to named approved entities.

evidence.provision: Preamble: Export Control Reform Act of 2018
evidence.quote: authorizes the regulation of exports, reexports, and transfers (in-country) of items subject to U.S. jurisdiction

summary.short: Final rule amending the Export Administration Regulations, effective 10 July 2026, to move the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 to Country Group A:5. License Exception STA becomes available for approved UAE government and commercial entities, and license requirements for advanced computing items to the UAE are kept except for approved recipients.
summary.long: Final rule of the Bureau of Industry and Security, effective 10 July 2026, amending the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR parts 740, 742 and 774) for the United Arab Emirates. It removes the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4, which lifts certain license-exception limits and missile-related end-use restrictions, and adds it to Country Group A:5. Under new § 740.2(a)(26), License Exception STA is available for UAE exports only to ultimate consignees and end users listed in new Supplement no. 8 to part 740. That supplement lists UAE government agencies (from 10 July 2026), two UAE-based AI companies, and named U.S.-headquartered AI companies and their UAE subsidiaries, which may receive advanced computing items license-free. The license requirement for advanced computing items to or within the UAE (§ 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(B)) is retained, except for these approved recipients. Other UAE entities may request an advisory opinion under § 748.3(c). The authorization for G42 and Core42 expires on 6 April 2027 absent notice by BIS. The rule also covers recordkeeping and Paperwork Reduction Act burden estimates and states that it is exempt from notice-and-comment requirements.

notes: Operative provisions are the amendments to sections 740.2(a)(26), supplement no. 1 to part 740 (Country Groups A:5 and D), supplement no. 8 to part 740, section 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(B) and the Commerce Control List in part 774; the Background and Summary are context only. Internal inconsistencies: DATES states effective July 10, 2026, but the document is dated as published in the Federal Register on July 14, 2026, and several approvals are stated as of July 10, 2026. Supplement no. 8, Note 2 to paragraph (b), says the G42 and Core42 authorization shall automatically expire on April 6, 2027 absent subsequent BIS notice, while the preamble says the two UAE-based AI companies must apply under section 748.3(c) if they do not become U.S. companies by that date; the text does not reconcile these. The extracted supplement no. 8 tables are partly garbled (addresses shown as [RESERVED]); assignment of entities to paragraph (b) or (c) follows the paragraph references in the text. Approval in supplement no. 8 does not override end-use and end-user requirements in part 744. Authority citations list further executive orders and presidential notices, not coded individually. The May 2025 U.S.-UAE AI cooperation framework is mentioned only in the summary and is not coded.

thresholds.note: No operative numeric cutoff in this text changes legal treatment. Day counts (30 and 5 days), the April 6, 2027 expiry, dollar figures and the 50-applications-per-year estimate are events, procedural limits or PRA estimates, not thresholds. The 300 km missile-range cutoff appears only in the preamble description of the prior regime, not in operative text. Advanced computing parameters are incorporated by ECCN paragraph references that are not reproduced here.

enforcement.note: The text states no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking for violating the license requirements it amends. It mentions a 'Enforcement of License Requirements for Advanced Computing Items' heading, but that section describes licence requirements and approvals, not sanctions. Rulemaking item 2 says no person is subject to a penalty for failing to respond to an information collection lacking an OMB control number; this is a penalty exemption, not a sanction regime, so it is not coded.
